content:
Every error response uses a single JSON envelope with a nested `error` object. Switch on the machine-readable `error.code`, not on the human message text.


## Response body

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `error.code` | string | Stable, machine-readable error code. Switch on this. | `"subscriber_not_found"` |
| `error.message` | string | Human-readable description. On `validation_failed` it always names the specific problem and field. On `401` / `403` it is deliberately terse (see the note under Codes) — switch on `error.code`, never on this text. | `"subscriberNumber must be at most 32 characters"` |
| `error.details` | array | Present on `validation_failed` only: one entry per rejected field, `\{field, message, rule, param?\}`. `rule` is the validation rule that failed (`required`, `uuid`, `max`, `unknown_field`, …) and `param` carries the bound when the rule has one. Absent on every other error code. | `[\{"field":"subscriberNumber","message":"subscriberNumber must be at most 32 characters","rule":"max","param":"32"\}]` |
| `traceId` | string | Request trace id (sibling of `error`). Include it when contacting support. | `"8b23d81344dbdcd29f92ddf26c4a2a07"` |

The HTTP status is carried on the response status line (not repeated in the body).

Example — a missing required field. `error.message` names it, and `error.details` carries the machine-readable entry:

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_failed",
    "message": "subscriberNumber is required",
    "details": [
      { "field": "subscriberNumber", "message": "subscriberNumber is required", "rule": "required" }
    ]
  },
  "traceId": "8b23d81344dbdcd29f92ddf26c4a2a07"
}
```

Example — a field that broke a bounded rule. `param` carries the bound:

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_failed",
    "message": "subscriberNumber must be at most 32 characters",
    "details": [
      { "field": "subscriberNumber", "message": "subscriberNumber must be at most 32 characters", "rule": "max", "param": "32" }
    ]
  },
  "traceId": "8b23d81344dbdcd29f92ddf26c4a2a07"
}
```

Example — a request body containing a property outside the documented schema. Unknown properties are rejected, not ignored, and the rejected name is echoed back:

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_failed",
    "message": "bogus is not a field of this request",
    "details": [
      { "field": "bogus", "message": "bogus is not a field of this request", "rule": "unknown_field" }
    ]
  },
  "traceId": "8b23d81344dbdcd29f92ddf26c4a2a07"
}
```

Example — a `403` from the API gateway. Note the terse message: branch on `error.code`.

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "insufficient_scope",
    "message": "insufficient permissions"
  },
  "traceId": "8b23d81344dbdcd29f92ddf26c4a2a07"
}
```


## Codes

| HTTP | `error.code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation_failed` | A field failed validation, a path/query parameter (e.g. `id`, `cursor`) is malformed, or the request body contains a property outside the documented schema (unknown fields are rejected, not ignored). `error.message` always names the specific problem, and `error.details` lists one entry per rejected field. |
| 400 | `service_plan_archived` | Attempted to assign an archived service plan. |
| 400 | `validation_failed` | Also covers **list query params**: `limit`/`pageSize` outside 1–500 (non-numeric, below 1, or above 500 — nothing is clamped, the error names the bound), a malformed `planId`, a bad `sort` field, a non-boolean `suspended`, or a malformed `cursor`. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing, malformed, unknown, expired, or revoked API key. Message is the terse `"unauthorized"`. |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | The key does not carry the scope required by the endpoint. Message is the terse `"insufficient permissions"`. |
| 404 | `subscriber_not_found` | Unknown subscriber id — or the subscriber is out of scope for a group-restricted key (indistinguishable, by design). |
| 404 | `service_plan_not_found` | Unknown service plan id. |
| 409 | `gateway_already_linked` | `PUT /subscribers/\{id\}/host`: the gateway host is already linked to **another** subscriber in this org. |
| 409 | `gateway_already_attached` | `PUT /subscribers/\{id\}/host`: the host is already attached to **this** subscriber, so there is nothing to do. The attach is not idempotent — nothing was written. Treat as "already applied" if you are retrying. |
| 409 | `no_attached_host` | `DELETE /subscribers/\{id\}/host`: the subscriber has no attached gateway host, so there is nothing to detach. The detach is not idempotent — nothing was written. Treat as "already applied" if you are retrying. |
| 400 | `host_not_in_organization` | `PUT /subscribers/\{id\}/host`: the host has no UniFi Network site in this organization, so a subscriber's service plan could never reach it. Attach a gateway running UniFi Network — a storage- or Protect-only console cannot carry a subscriber. |
| 429 | `too_many_requests` | Rate limit exceeded — see the `Retry-After` header and retry after the delay. Nothing was processed, so the request is safe to resend unchanged. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | Unexpected server error. The request may or may not have been applied — re-read the resource before retrying a write. Cite `traceId` to support if it persists. |
| 503 | `write_conflict_retryable` | Your request collided with a concurrent update to the same subscriber and the whole transaction was rolled back, so **nothing was changed**. Retry the identical request — it normally succeeds immediately. There is nothing to correct in the request; this is not a validation problem. |
| 503 | `host_directory_unavailable` | `PUT /subscribers/\{id\}/host`: the gateway-host directory could not be reached, so we cannot verify the host belongs to your organization. The attach was refused rather than accepted on an unverified host. Retry shortly. |


### Which errors are safe to retry

|  | Safe to resend the identical request? |
| --- | --- |
| `429 too_many_requests` | **Yes**, after `Retry-After`. Nothing was processed. |
| `503 write_conflict_retryable` | **Yes**, immediately. The transaction rolled back; nothing was written. |
| `503 host_directory_unavailable` | **Yes**, shortly. The attach was refused, not partially applied. |
| `500 internal_error` | **Only after re-reading.** The write may or may not have landed. |
| every `4xx` above | **No** — fix the request (or, for the two 409s, treat as already applied). |

**401 and 403 are produced by the API gateway, before the request reaches the Subscriber API.** That is why their
`error.message` is short (`"unauthorized"`, `"insufficient permissions"`) while every other code carries a descriptive
message. Branch on `error.code`; do not match on message text.

Validation (`400 validation_failed`) is all-or-nothing — nothing is created or changed; fix the field named in `error.details` (or `error.message` when it is specific) and resend the same call.

See [Getting Started](https://developer.ui.com/carrier-fabric/v1.0.0/getting-started) for authentication and scopes, and [Examples](https://developer.ui.com/carrier-fabric/v1.0.0/examples) for successful-flow walkthroughs.
